flags.name: Herb Coriander 5-6 M/B
flags.issue: MARKET BUNCH COSTED AS A SINGLE BUNCH. The feed carries pack_qty 1, pack_unit 'bunch', $9.40 per bunch, needs_pack_review FALSE — so nothing else will surface it. The supplier's own description says '5-6 M/B' (five to six market bunches) and the invoice's raw_uom is BUNCH, which is what made it look like one. CONFIRMED, NOT GUESSED, from our own paperwork: on the SAME DAY (invoice 3054116, 2026-06-12) Select Fresh billed code HCOR 'HERB CORIANDER BCH' at $1.50 a bunch, and 3068987 (2026-06-27) at $1.30. $9.40 / $1.50 = 6.3, consistent with 5-6 bunches. A recipe that calls for one bunch of coriander and picks this row books 6-7x its true cost. This is the triage-log item-13 pattern exactly (FFT HCB $2.64 single vs HCDRMB $9.90-$15.40 market bunch), on a different supplier.
flags.suggested_fix: Do NOT divide by a guessed count — the supplier states a RANGE (5-6), so no single divisor is confirmable, and inventing one is how a 12x error gets shipped. Two safe options for Zak: (a) disambiguate the name the way item 13 does for FFT, e.g. 'Herb Coriander Market Bunch (HCORM)', so the chef can see it is not the same thing as HCOR; or (b) if Zak confirms the count on a delivery, add a pack_overrides entry 'select-fresh:HCORM' with that count in ea. Until then the pickable coriander should stay select-fresh:HCOR / lightspeed:22995344 ($1.30-$1.50 a bunch, already a confirmed bridge).

flags.name: Corn Chips Rosita Tri
flags.issue: NAME TRUNCATED — the pack size and brand are missing. The full description is on our own invoice SI4457228 (2026-07-10): 'CORN CHIPS ROSITA TRI 6X500GM Mission'. The two later invoices (SI4467596 2026-07-16 and SI4507196 2026-08-06) both print the short form because the description wrapped and the pre-2026-08-17 Foodlink parser dropped the continuation row — the triage-log item-33 defect. build_ingredients keys names by (identity, code) and takes the code's LATEST name, so the truncated spelling wins. _undo_dropped_prefix cannot repair it: that rule matches a dropped LEADING word by suffix, and this is a dropped TRAILING word (the item 23/32 asymmetry). THE COST IS NOT AFFECTED — pack_qty is 3000 g via a chef-confirmed override, which is exactly 6 x 500 g, so $47.30 / 3 kg = $0.015767/g is right. This is identity and legibility, not money.
flags.suggested_fix: No edit made and none needed by hand: the item-33 parser fix shipped 2026-08-17, so the NEXT Foodlink delivery of 100831 should re-read the full 'CORN CHIPS ROSITA TRI 6X500GM Mission' and the fullest-name consolidation should heal it on its own. Recorded here so that if it is still truncated in a week, the reason to look is this entry. Same expectation as item 23.

Packaging in the ingredient picker is BY DESIGN — item 11 — this is how Marilyna's per-box cost is tracked, so it is not a category error.

Not applied here — this is a review, not a silent change, and pack_overrides in 'ea' is the count branch that item 26 showed must be applied carefully.

mentions.name: Postmix BIBs (Pepsi Max 10L, Pepsi 15L, Schweppes Tonic 10L, Lemonade 15L, Red Cream Soda 15L)
mentions.issue: NOT FLAGGED AS AN ERROR, and this is deliberate. All five landed on 2026-08-19 as declared costs at an identical $0.030029/ml, which looks like a division that did not happen — it is not: the 10L rows are $272.99/case ex and the 15L rows $409.49/case ex, i.e. the same $27.30/L, so the arithmetic is internally consistent and the pack division IS being applied. The row's own note records the source and the human confirmation: 'CUB cart 2026-08-19, $409.49/case ex GST, 1 BIB per case (Zak)'. The one thing worth a second look, stated without guessing at a replacement: $27.30/L ex for post-mix syrup is high against what these BIBs have historically listed for, and the single input that would explain it is the BIBS-PER-CASE figure — if a CUB cart line is a case of two or three BIBs, the per-ml rate is 2-3x too dear. It errs in the CONSERVATIVE direction (it understates GP, which is the safe way to be wrong per CLAUDE.md), it is Zak-confirmed and dated, so NOTHING was changed. Worth 30 seconds against the CUB cart next order.
